caption: The Ashen Knight's reveal roar on the merged FistAim grip (GL, hour 8.5, from behind): the left fist flung up reads, but the right fist on the glaive is hidden behind the cape from this lens, so the grip is not yet judged; backlit, dark armour.

The Ashen Knight with its glaive in the late sun beside the cottage: the fists sit on the haft (bot 0.000 m), but the hand lens frames it wide and the gloved right fist is lost in shadow under the pauldron.

The reveal's kneeling coil from the intro lens: a good ring of standing stones and god-lit meadow, but the lens sits behind the knight so the hands on the glaive (now held 1.9 cm off the haft) never show, and the figure is a dark silhouette.

The Ashen Knight's crown reel 0.42 s in: head bowed, the left hand let go of the glaive and cups the left side of the helm (wrist 4 cm per size off the temple, bot-gated); from this low front-left lens the gauntlet is half hidden behind the red hood and the glaive tilts one-handed, so the clutch reads only weakly.
The same crown-reel frame with the old pose (CROWN_NOCLUTCH=1): both fists stay down on the haft, so the stunned knight reads as a hunch; kept for comparison with the clutch frame.

Ashen Knight crown reel at the clutch's landing overshoot (u 0.24), new chest-height lens on its left: too close, the bowed helm and pauldron hide the gauntlet entirely, so the eased landing cannot be judged from here.

The Ashen Knight kneeling dazed in the crown reel from a new wide chest-height lens: the whole body reads in the ring, but the lens is on its right side so the hand clutching the helm is hidden behind it.

The Ashen Knight in the crown daze, low lens from its front left: the gauntlet now sits up on the helm (the bow runs before the arm IK, palm 0.001 m per size off the temple, was 0.044); still backlit to a silhouette so the hand only reads as a shape.
The knight lifting the glaive out of the daze (u 0.68): the right fist stays on the haft through the rise (worst 0.030 m per size, was 0.096); the low backlit lens still hides the hands' detail.

The Ashen Knight heaving its glaive skyward as it grows in the surge (low flank lens, GL): the right fist now holds the haft through the roar (worst 0.144 m per size, was 0.31) and the left closes back on it cleanly; the frame shows the knight hanging above the turf and the glaive lost against the sky, a lens/harness problem to fix next.
The same surge frame with the old grip switch (SURGE_ROLLOFF=1) for comparison: at this lens the fist change is not visible, and the same floating knight and backlit silhouette make it a fail.

The Ashen Knight's growth-surge roar with its new pose: the glaive stands tall in front of it, the right fist held out on the haft at chest height (fist-haft gap 0.000 m per size, was 0.144); the ring of fire hides most of the body and the light is flat, so not yet a Wukong frame.
The same surge frame with the old roar pose (SURGE_OLDROAR=1): the right fist jammed up against the shoulder, the arm folded shut, which is what rolled the fist off the haft.
The Ashen Knight's reveal follow-through: the glaive now comes down held out in front of the chest with both fists on the haft; the armour still reads dark and flat at this distance.
Before: the right arm jammed against the shoulder and the shaft sliding past the fist as the glaive comes down.

The Ashen Knight a tick after its reveal roar ends, glaive held upright with both fists on the haft; the 10-degree jump of the glaive here is gone (motion only, the frame looks the same). Still wrong: seen from behind, armour dark and flat, the shaft thin.

The Ashen Knight at the end of its reveal roar: the glaive now hangs upright out at its right with both gauntlets on the haft before speeding into the downswing (no more stall); the armour still reads dark and flat and the ground is speckled.
Before: the same tick with the old follow-through, the left grip past its reach so the haft slants across the body and the swing stalls for a tick.

The Hollow Soldier at rest in its re-solved guard (left; GL renderer): the spear now lies where its pose says, the frame matches the old look; still flat GL light, a small, backlit figure, not a Wukong frame.

The Harrier (right) at rest in its re-solved low guard: the spear on the line it visibly held, both fists inside reach so every move out of the guard starts clean; still too far and dark to read the hands, grass flat-lit.
Before: the same frame with the old low guard (the pose asked a grip past its reach, the real shaft 20 deg off its pose); near-identical at rest, the difference shows in the moves out of it.

The harrier at full stretch of its dart: the spear now drives forward and low past the hero's waist along the dart's line (bot foereach 0.0 deg); still shot from behind the hero, so the foe is half hidden.
Before: the same frame with the old dart pose, the front grip clamped 0.5 m short so the spear stood straight up, 96 deg off the line it was meant to drive along.

The Hollow Soldier mid-sweep with its hands no longer flapping on the spear tick to tick (a frozen frame can't show the fix, the bot measures it); the hero's back hides the foe's hands and the grass reads oversaturated.
The Hollow soldier's thrust at full stretch now drives the spear level along the blow's line into the hero; still wrong: the two bodies overlap from this side-on lens and the foe's hands are hidden.
Before: the same thrust frame with the old pose, the front grip past its reach so the spear stood straight up, 102 deg off the line of the blow.
Hollow Hewer mid-raise: the axe now swings up in an arc out in front of the body instead of dragging up the chest; still backlit and far, the grips can't be judged at this distance.
Hollow Hewer at the top of its raise: fists before the face, the axe cocked back over the head (arms no longer folded shut); the hewer is a dark silhouette, the lens too wide.

The shield warden's re-solved bash coil: spear angled up from the hauled-back right fist, elbow out, fist on the haft. Still wrong: backlit against the sun, the hood and arms read as a dark silhouette at this distance.
Before (BASH_OLD=1): the old coil laid the spear flat across the chest, bent 7 deg through the reach clamp; same dark backlit framing.

The harrier's overrun after its dart with the re-solved pose: the rear fist drawn back to the hip instead of crushed up under the armpit; the lens is placed for the crouch, so the harrier sits on the frame's edge overlapping the hero and the arm cannot be graded.
Before: the same overrun frame with the old pose, the spear tucked up under the right arm (shoulder-to-wrist 0.111 m); same poor framing.

The harrier's crouch at the hero's back with the re-solved spear pose (shaft now on its pose, no clamp bend into the dart); the harrier is still backlit and dark, the arms cannot be read at this lens.
The Ashen Knight at the leap's take-off (the shot harness stops at the strike's first tick, so the re-solved heave is not in frame); fog and bloom wash the knight out to a white silhouette.

The Ashen Knight at the top of its ember leap, legs tucked and the glaive heaved over its right shoulder (re-solved arc, now seen in a real frame sequence); lit and readable, but the shot harness leaves it at phase-1 size during a phase-2 move and the lens sits a little behind its shoulder.

The knight falling onto the hero with the glaive swung out level in front and the legs reaching down for the landing; the down arc reads, the giant still looks too small next to the hero for a phase-2 leap.
The blade biting the turf in front of the hero as the knight lands; a coherent end to the arc, armour materials and the grass still short of a Wukong frame.

The phase-2-sized knight (x3.2) in mid-leap above the village, glaive heaved over its right shoulder with both fists on the haft; the arc reads, armour and cloth still read flat and dark for a Wukong frame.
The giant falling at the small hero (bottom left) with the glaive swung out level; the size gap finally reads as a boss leap, but the body is stiff and the lighting flat.
The blade biting the turf beside the hero as the giant lands; the torso stays upright instead of bending into the slam, so the impact lacks weight.

The Ashen Knight a beat after the ember leap's bite: knees given deep, chest pitched over the glaive in the turf (was stiff and upright). Still wrong: rear three-quarter lens foreshortens the pitch; armour reads flat in the GL fallback renderer.
The knight holding its crouch over the bitten blade before wrenching it free, boots planted. Still wrong: no dust kicked off the knees and grass not flattened round the boots.

Front-quarter lens on the Ashen Knight at the bottom of its ember-leap landing: knees given, chest over the bitten glaive, a pale ring of dust rolling off the right boot. Still wrong: the ember-ring flame stands right in front of the boot and hides half the kick, and the GL fallback renders the armour flat.

The same front-quarter lens a beat earlier: the giant bottoming out over its blade, the hero a third of its height at left. Still wrong: tall grass hides the boots and the clods read as tiny specks at this scale.

Ashen Knight's leap landing at phase-2 size: the ember ring now flares to the sides and ahead of the bite, the boot and its dust kick read clear; the front flame still crosses the front-quarter lens and the GL renderer is flat.
Before: the old ring phase stood a flame right on the knight's own boot, hiding the landing's dust kick.
The Ashen Knight (phase-1 size) at its re-solved guard behind the hero; the glaive line reads, but the knight is a backlit dark silhouette and the shot is software-rendered (no GI/volumetrics).

Before (left, shared guard) / after (right, guard re-solved against the knight's real shoulders): the glaive sits ~10 cm higher and closer at this size, the right elbow keeps a bend; a barely visible change, mainly a correctness fix.

The Ashen Knight's reveal heave, now posed from its real shoulders: both fists on the glaive, drawn up diagonally over the right shoulder; the knight still reads dark against the sun and the shadowed turf is flat.

Reveal coil from the front: the glaive held level at the hip with the left fist now visibly on the haft (before it trailed on the turf with that fist off it); the coil reads a little less low than before.

The Ashen Knight crouched over its bitten glaive after the ember leap: both fists now drawn in to the chest with the elbows bent (before, the left arm locked straight along the haft); still backlit and dark against the sun, the knight reads small at this distance.
The Ashen Knight coiled for its sweep with the left elbow now bent: the glaive rides high out past the right pauldron; seen from behind, so the arms themselves are hidden.
The first tick of the knight's sweep cut, the glaive swinging out level over the hero; the lens is too close for the 2.2x giant and crops the helm.

The Ashen Knight coiled for its sweep, seen at last from its own front-right quarter (new kchest lens): the raised glaive passes clear of the helm at shoulder height, but the backlit armour hides the arms.
The start of the knight's sweep cut from its front quarter: the glaive comes down diagonally across the body in both fists; still backlit and the giant reads dark against the meadow.

The Ashen Knight's sweep coil finally lit from its front (16:30 sun): helm, gorget and right pauldron read; but the glaive runs in behind the right pauldron and through the lower skirt of the helm at the throat (measured 0.17 m/size deep), and the left arm is hidden.

The ember leap's heave in mid-air: the glaive's haft passes straight through the crown of the knight's great helm (measured 0.16-0.18 m/size deep through the whole held heave); needs a new heave line beside the helm.

The ember leap's hang, re-solved: the glaive is heaved over the knight's left shoulder, blade high behind, and the haft now clears the great helm by 0.056 m/size for the whole hang; still seen only from behind, so the hands and elbows cannot be judged.

The ember leap's rise: the glaive comes up beside the helm into the sky instead of through its crown; the shared crouch still grazes the helm's back rim on take-off and the landing passes under its flared rim.
The Ashen Knight's leap crouch now raises its glaive near-upright in front of the helm, both fists on the haft and clear of the helm; the helm still reads as a dark dome with no face from this lens.

The Ashen Knight lands its ember leap bowed over the bitten glaive, the haft now running out past its helm into the turf instead of up under the rim; the helm still reads as a dark dome and the sky is too dark for the hour.
Frame 9 of the first 12-frame sequence of the Ashen Knight's ember leap: glaive bitten into the turf by the hero, ember ring flaring; the knight is still small in frame and its helm reads faceless.
The knight's push-off now rises smoothly out of the deeper crouch instead of snapping up 1.3 m in one tick; the cottage roof hides the legs from this lens.

Ashen Knight ember leap down-swing, top row old timing (blade already in the turf while the giant still hangs ~2 m up), bottom row new (blade still high, level near the ground, bites as the boots land); still backlit from this lens, the helm reads as a dark dome.
The knight's glaive whipping level over the hero a beat before the bite; motion reads, but the knight is a dark silhouette against the sun and the grass/cottage are still prototype-grade beside it.

The Ashen Knight coils its sweep with the glaive now passing under its helm's chin skirt (bot: clear by 0.125 m/size, was 0.17 through); the knight is still dim and backlit, and the helm reads as a dark dome.

Before (left) the coiled haft ran into the helm's lower edge; after (right) it runs lower under the chin to the right fist with the chest turned further into the coil. A small change at this distance.
The Ashen Knight's sweep two ticks off the held coil: the glaive now accelerates out of the coil instead of popping to full speed; the knight is still small and backlit from this lens.
The sweep's glaive whipping low across the knight's front at peak speed past the hero; the motion reads, the framing and dark backlit armour do not hold up as a Wukong shot yet.

A Hollow Soldier's sweep at bearing +48 deg seen past the hero's straw cape: the cut now runs out without the follow-through hitch, but the figures are small in a wide sunlit field and the lens is too far to read the swing.
Same sweep at +62 deg from behind the soldier: hat, cloak and red tabard read well in warm light, but a straw sheaf blocks the hero and the spear is a thin line against the grass.

The Ashen Knight at the top of its ember leap seen square from the side: the glaive lies back ~40 deg over the shoulder with both fists overhead and knees tucked; backlit from this side and a GL frame, not Forward+.

The whole ember leap from a fixed side lens (crouch, rise over the cottage, hang, down-swing, bite): the arc height and lay-back now read; the crouch is hidden behind the cottage and the knight is backlit.
The boss at the top of its ember leap with the glaive now laid ~60 deg back behind its shoulders; still backlit and small in frame from this side lens.

Before (top) / after (bottom) of the leap's heave and hang: the hang lays the glaive much further back and the butt no longer swings through the left shoulder as deep; the landing frames leave the crop.

The boss holding its sweep's coil, glaive cocked back at its right shoulder; the haft's butt now passes behind the left pauldron instead of into it, but the knight is backlit and the change is barely readable at this distance.
Before (left) / after (right) crop of the sweep coil: the hold sits a little lower and further back; a closer side lens is still needed to show the pauldron clearance.

The Ashen Knight's held sweep coil through the new side lens: glaive cocked level behind its right side over the meadow; the lens drifts off square once it turns to the hero, and the far field still looks flat.

Sweep follow-through, before (top) / after (bottom): the hold now runs out further left and forward; this lens lands behind the knight, so the right-pauldron clearance is proven by the bot, not by these frames.

Hero's feet mid standing turn, old ankle pivot (left) vs new ball pivot with heel lifted (middle, right); the change is subtle and the hero stands in the barn's shade, so a sunlit sequence is still needed.
First low lens on the boots through a 160 deg turn on the spot (0.40-1.60 s): step arc and closed end stance read, but it is dark and unlit.

The Ashen Knight (phase-1 size) mid turn on the spot at 09:00, low boot lens: the planted boot now stands on its ball with the heel up instead of spinning flat; the lens still crops the body and the boots read small.
Same tick before the change (FOEBALL_OLD=1): the planted boot lies flat and pivots on its ankle; for comparison only.

The phase-3 Ashen Knight (size 4.6) squaring up after a turn on the spot: the heel now stays on the ball and the hips ease up instead of slapping flat and popping; the pop was 1-4 ticks so this still frame looks the same as before; the knight reads small from this lens.
The giant knight mid-turn on the ball of its planted foot, glaive raised; feet planted, but the low lens and grass in the foreground crowd the frame.

New sun-bearing ankle lens on the hero's turn on the spot (0.1 s in): boots lit and readable for the first time; the baggy trouser hem hangs over the stepping boot almost to the turf and hides the heel.
Same turn 0.25 s in: the planted boot sits on its ball under the tabard; heel lift is too subtle to read at 13 deg and the radial trample decal around the feet looks stamped.
The hero's boots mid turn on the spot, heel now rising 5.5 cm onto the ball; the tabard hem hides the heel and the radial trample decal looks stamped.
Hero's boots in a turn on the spot: the stamped radial starburst of combed straw under the feet is gone; the tabard hem still hides the pivot heel and the turf reads flat at this range.
A trodden lane through the meadow: the matted sward now combs in a wandering swirl instead of ruled lines; the laid lane is still too smooth and uniform in colour.

Turn on the spot at jt 0.55, sunlit ankle lens: the hips now rise with the heel on the ball, so the boots sit under a less folded knee; the baggy trouser hem still swallows the boot and the GL ground reads flat.
Before (left) vs after (right) at jt 0.55: the robe hem sits slightly higher as the body rises on the pivot ball; the difference is small from this low lens, a side-on full-body lens is still owed.

Turn on the spot at jt 0.40 from the new full-body side lens (sidelens prof bodytight): the step back and the ball pivot read, the hips stay up; the hero's front is in its own shade and the shin wraps read as bulky tubes.

Turn on the spot at jt 0.55, side-on full body: with the hips hold the whole figure stands a few px taller than the old build (hat brim higher); the knees are still hidden under robe and tabard and the GL ground reads flat.

Hero's boots in a turn on the spot: the shins are now bound tight and the puttee stops at the instep so the leather boots show; still a grey greave plate peeks at the ankle and the back ankle band shows a hollow rim.
Full-body side view mid-turn with the slimmer shin bindings; the legs no longer read as a bulky tube, but the hero's front sits in self-shade from this side.

Ankle lens in a turn on the spot: the boots' grey heel counter and ankle straps are now worn strap leather, no grey plate between binding and boot; specular glints on the boot toe and the ground texture still look synthetic.
Full-body side view mid-turn: the feet now read as dark leather boots; the hero still lacks Wukong-grade detail (flat hat, thin capelet, stiff robe panel) and the ground is a flat ochre plane.

Ankle lens through a turn on the spot: the boots' toe caps are now scuffed matte brown leather instead of glossy pink lacquer; the trouser hem is still baggy and the ground texture reads flat in the GL fallback renderer.
The hero side-on in the meadow by the cottage at 09:00; the boots are lost in the grass at this distance, and the figure and lighting still read as a GL-compatibility render, not Wukong.

New sunside lens: the hero's turn on the spot as a front 3/4 on the sun's flank at 09:00; feet, staff and face read, but the front still sits half in shade (the sun is behind him here) and the face is a flat pink mask.
Same moment through the old square profile lens for comparison: the hero's front is in self-shade and the legs hide behind the tabard.

Hero's turn on the spot at 9:00, mid-turn, judged front-lit for the first time (new facesun option): face and cape lit, both fists on the staff. Still wrong: the feet cross into a scissor stance, the face reads as a flat pale mask.
Hero's left turn on the spot at 0.45/0.55/0.65 s: the feet stay apart and the stepping leg passes behind, no scissor; still the knees nearly touch mid-step and the body tilts hard sideways.
Same instant before (left, feet crossed into a scissor stance) and after the fix (right, stepping foot held on its own side).

The hero mid-turn to the left on the ball of the foot, now standing a little taller with the stepping boot lifted 4 cm instead of 6.5; the knees still read knock-kneed and the face is a flat pale mask.
Hero mid-way through a turn on the spot to the left, weight now slid over the planted foot; the legs still read crossed from this lens and the face is a flat flesh-coloured plane.

Turn on the spot to the left, 0.1 s in: the forward guard boot now draws in toward the body before the hero pivots on it; the knees still hide under the robe and the light is flat ochre, not Wukong-grade.
Walking up a 3 x 0.2 m stair: the swinging boot now lifts with the knee raised over the riser instead of running into it; lens is low and side-on, test stair is plain boxes.
Same frame before the change (STEPCLEAR_OLD): both legs nearly straight, the lead boot driven into the riser face.
Three ticks later: the trailing boot is lifted while still behind the hips, so the shin folds up flat behind the body; next fix.

Hero climbing the test stair: the hips now rise over the lead foot on the first tread instead of squatting; still seen from behind with hat and robe hiding the knees, and the steps are plain test boxes.
Same stair frame before (left: crouched to the trailing tread) and after (right: standing taller over the lead foot); the lens is still poor for judging the knees.

Left turn on the spot, before/after at 0.40 s and 0.55 s (old, new, old, new): the forward foot is now drawn in under the hips before the spin, so the hero stays upright instead of leaning hard over a far-off pivot; knees still close and hidden by the robe.
Mid-turn on the spot at 9:00 with the full gather step: feet under the body and the hero no longer drifts off; the pose still reads stiff and knock-kneed, flat light on the legs.
Walking up the stair, second step: before (left) the lead boot sank into the tread as the body stepped up, now (right) it stands on it; still plain box steps and a low fixed lens.
The hero steps up at a walk, near boot on the tread top; the stair is untextured-looking masonry boxes and the lens loses him by the top.
The hero walking off a low masonry course, lead boot reaching heel-first for the turf: the step reads, but the light is flat, the course is a plain box and the robe hides the knees.

Hero walking up the test stair side-on at the step-up tick: the hips now keep the walk's pace instead of lurching 12 cm onto the tread; still plain box steps, a dark flat foreground and the hat and robe hiding the knees.

A Hollow soldier now walks up a three-tread stone stair at a stalk, mid-climb on the second tread; still wrong: the test stair is a plain box course, and the soldier is backlit and dark against the low sun.
Before the fix (same moment): the soldier is stuck against the first riser, lifting and falling back every tick; foes could never climb a stair at a stalk.
The hero walking down the 3-tread test stair, rear boot on the upper tread and the lead boot set on the next; the lens crops the hat and the stair is a plain test block on flat turf.
Wider 3/4 front view of the same descent at the step-down tick: both boots stand on their treads, but the figure is small, the light flat, and the stair a bare test block.

A Hollow soldier walking up the 3-tread test stair, both boots on the stone, its body no longer trailing its collision capsule by half a metre; still a bare test block and flat afternoon light, not a real place.

A Hollow soldier walking down the test stair at a stalk, one boot on each tread now that the foot IK uses the eased step dip; still a plain box stair on an empty meadow under flat GL light, and the hero stands visible behind it.
The same soldier stepping off the last tread onto the turf without a pop; the GL fallback lighting is flat and the scene is a test set, not a Wukong frame.
The Ashen Knight at its phase-3 size (4.6x) on the test stair on open meadow: lens too low and backlit, its head cropped out, the stair a plain dark box with no masonry.

The Ashen Knight at its phase-1 size walking onto the test stair after the boot-height fix; backlit silhouette and the stair top hides its boots, so the fix (boots no longer 2-11 cm into the turf) cannot be judged here, and the stair is still a plain dark slab.

The hero jogging across the meadow after the ankle/ball floor fix (boots no longer planted 4-6 cm into the ground, measured by bot heroflat); backlit and the tall grass hides the boots, so the frame cannot show the fix itself.

The Ashen Knight (x2.2) a tenth of a second into a stop from a walk, now stepping its boots into the guard stance instead of skating them (bot foestop: 0.24-0.80 -> 0.01 m/size); the lens is poor: a tree trunk fills the left, the knight is backlit and its boots sit in shadow, so the steps themselves are not visible.

The Ashen Knight at its phase-1 size stepping into its guard after a stop, lit from the sun side at 10:00; the meadow grass still hides its boots, so the settle-step fix only shows in the bot numbers, and the armour reads dark against the bright field.

A Hollow Soldier that walked in opens its thrust wind-up in the meadow grass (backlit, hour 10): drawn pose and lit chest embers read, but the foe is nearly a silhouette and the foreground blades are too broad.

Frames 50/58/62/72: the soldier walks, stops and draws its thrust; the boots take one settle step then hold still, but the hood crown reads as a stiff cylinder and the ground under the hidden grass is a flat straw texture.

The Hollow Soldier's hood from the fight camera's height after the reshape: a round crown on the skull, folds no longer meeting in a star at the tip; the cloth still looks too clean and smooth for ash-stiff hemp.
The hood from behind and above: a rounded crown widening steadily to the shoulders (it was a flat-lidded pail); still a too-regular bell over a mantle that reads as a pleated skirt shelf.

The Hollow Soldier's hood from the low fight-side view: the crown now rolls down over the brow like a head's curve and the lower hood breaks into a few irregular stiff folds; the side still reads as one broad flat-lit panel and the armour is a dull grey.
The hood from behind and above: a rounded crown falling in sharper-ridged hemp folds; the mantle under it still reads as a pleated skirt shelf.

Hollow Soldier from the fight camera: the hood's side now shows darkened fold hollows and sagging stiff creases instead of one flat-lit panel; the hemp still reads a bit pale and clean, and the meadow trees are blotchy.
Hood side close-up, before (left) and after (right): baked fold cavity shading plus horizontal crumple creases give the cloth form; the weave is still a uniform stripe pattern.

The hero 0.5 s after letting go at a walk: both boots set flat on the turf in the idle stance (the new walk stop, now on by default); backlit at midday beside the cottage, the legs read dark and the lens is behind the hero.
The hero 0.15 s into a run stop: front boot struck, back boot behind on the turf; the lens is low and backlit, the head is cropped and the raised left hand reads as a wave, not a balance swing.
0.65 s after letting go of a run: the settle has stepped both boots flat into the idle stance with no skate, but the frame is backlit, the legs are dark and the head is cut off by the lens.

The hero braking from a run, sunlit side-on: front boot struck and pinned on the turf, back boot on its ball, the balance hand forward at chest height; the hand still reads a little high and the legs dark under the tabard.
The same run stop settled 0.4 s later, boots together in the idle stance on a sunlit yard; pose reads, but the dark legs and the flat cottage behind keep it below a Wukong frame.
The hero letting go at a jog now plants: front heel struck, back boot on its ball, balance hand forward; the stop reads, but the legs are dark under the tabard and the yard is flat.
The same jog stop 0.2 s later, both boots flat and the body rising over them with no skate; lighting on the figure is still murky for a Wukong frame.
The hero stepping out of a fast-walk stop, seen three-quarter from behind; the stepped boot now lands on the turf, but the legs read as a dark mass under the tabard.
Settled after the walk stop: both boots flat on the turf in the idle stance (no hover); trousers and greaves still too dark even in sun.

The hero just after letting go at a fast walk: both boots set flat on the turf as the stop's pivot lets go (the 1-2 cm bob is gone); the legs still read dark under the tabard and the yard ground is flat and plain.
